summary: Backend smoke + happy-path tests for 13 newly scaffolded route modules (split_payment, loyalty, reviews, scheduled, subscriptions, safety, promo, filters, group_orders, quick_actions, tips_gifts, delivery_options, bnpl). 22/39 passed, 17 FAILED with 500 KeyError 'user_id'. Root cause: ALL new routes reference user['user_id'] / user['first_name'] / user['last_name'] but core.security.get_current_user() returns the raw Mongo user document which only has '_id' (ObjectId) and 'name'. This is a systemic scaffolding bug affecting every auth-protected new endpoint.

critical.issue: user['user_id'] KeyError -> 500. get_current_user returns raw Mongo doc with '_id' (ObjectId), not 'user_id'. Must use str(user['_id']) or normalize the user dict in get_current_user.
Code uses user['first_name'] / user['last_name'] which don't exist on user docs (only 'name'). Will 500 even after user_id is fixed.
Endpoint specified in PRD but not implemented (returns 405). Only /my-points, /add-points, /stamp, /leaderboard exist.
Endpoint specified in PRD but not implemented (returns 405). History array is stored on the loyalty doc but never exposed via GET.
Endpoint specified in PRD but not implemented in tips_gifts.py (returns 405). Only /give, /my-tips, /gift-card/* exist.
Designed as 'internal API' but exposed publicly without auth – any unauthenticated caller can grant points to any user_id. Add admin/internal-only guard.
Public endpoint leaks ride pickup/destination/rider_name without any access guard beyond knowing the share_id (UUID is fine but no expiry enforcement).
If service_type is neither 'taxi' nor 'food' the function returns None (FastAPI yields 'null'). Should 400.
Build error if promo doc has no 'code' key when filtering one_per_user (KeyError); also lookups are O(N) per request.

minor.issue: Crashes if any user has 0 points and last_name is empty: last_name[0] raises IndexError; also wraps {} dict for sorted level lookup that may pick wrong level when points exactly match boundary.
Accepts ISO without 'Z' but ambiguous timezone; relies on fromisoformat which differs across Python versions.
user_doc['created_at'] required - registration may not always set it, raising KeyError.
user.get('last_name', '')[0] crashes when last_name is empty string.
all_confirmed math is wrong: len(confirmed_by) == len(participants)+1 but organizer is already in confirmed_by AND not in participants -> off-by-one when organizer self-joins.

action_items: URGENT: Fix get_current_user (or all 13 new routes) so user['user_id'] resolves. Recommended: in core/security.py get_current_user, set user['user_id'] = str(user['_id']) before returning. This single change fixes 80% of failures.

Fix references to user['first_name'] / user['last_name'] in split_payment.py, safety.py, group_orders.py, tips_gifts.py, reviews.py, loyalty.py - admin/seeded users only have 'name'. Use user.get('name','User').split()[0] or user.get('first_name') or user.get('name','User').
Implement the 3 missing endpoints listed in PRD: GET /api/loyalty/levels, GET /api/loyalty/history, GET /api/tips/presets.
Add auth+admin guard on POST /api/loyalty/add-points (currently public, can be abused).
Fix off-by-one in group_orders.join confirmation count.
Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_new_routes.py after fixes - this regression suite covers smoke + happy paths.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Root failure across new routes is user['user_id'] KeyError. Once main agent normalizes get_current_user to inject user_id=str(_id) (and adds first_name fallback to name), re-run pytest /app/backend/tests/test_new_routes.py. Then add deeper tests with real ride/order seed data for happy-path split-payment/tips/bnpl flows. Login uses httpOnly cookie 'access_token'; tests work around this by extracting cookie value and passing as Bearer.
rca of the issue: core/security.py::get_current_user returns the raw users-collection document (keys: _id, email, name, role, ...). The 13 new route files were written assuming a normalized dict with keys user_id/first_name/last_name. Every protected endpoint that does user['user_id'] therefore raises KeyError and FastAPI's global exception handler converts it to 500 {'detail': "'user_id'"}. Mitigation: in get_current_user, just before return, do user['user_id'] = str(user['_id']) and split user.get('name','') into first_name/last_name. Single-point fix unblocks the majority of new routes.
